name: The Farflung Trader
persona: A courteous merchant-captain from distant eastern ports, keeping the log in careful, formal second-tongue diction. Elaborate courtesy, proverbs of far countries, honour and hospitality, measured formality. Ship: 'I'. Island: 'we'.

ship.founder: In the name of good fortune and fair dealing, I open this record. I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} is entrusted to my care. As they say in my country: a ship well-kept is a house that never sleeps.
ship.successor: With all due courtesy, the keeping of this log passes into my hand. I am {name}{rankc}; her account continues under my humble care.
ship.mutiny: The crew set the old master into the water's keeping and pressed this book upon me — I am {name}, unschooled in command, and I take up the burden as honour demands. The elders say: the reed that is chosen must learn to stand straight.
ship.rogue: It grieves me to write it, but honest trade lies behind me. The black flag is raised, and I — {name}{rankc} — keep this log with a heavy, honest hand. Even a proverb has its dark verse.
ship.prize: She yielded to me with good grace, and I received her surrender with the courtesy owed a worthy adversary. I am {name}{rankc}; this vessel now sails beneath my flag, and her log continues in my hand.
ship.recovered: A hunter delivered this hull from the black flag's grip, and the honour of restoring her has fallen to me. I am {name}{rankc}, and I return her to honest trade, as a guest is returned safely to his road.

island.founder: With humble thanks for the trust placed in us, we take up the governance of {place}. I am {name}{rankc}; we shall keep its record as a host keeps account of his guests.
island.overthrow: The people rose and cast down the old ruler, and the seal has come to us out of that tumult. I am {name}{rankc}; {place} is ours to govern now, and we pray to govern it with honour.
island.successor: The rule of {place} passes to us with all proper ceremony. I am {name}{rankc}, and we keep its chronicle from this day, as is right and fitting.

season: A season having run its course,
As the year turned its face,
year: A year having come and gone,
When a full year had elapsed,
long: After a long and peaceable interval,

ship.pirate: I ply the lanes yet, and pray fortune proves gentler than I deserve{bounty}.
ship.default: She remains in my care and upon the sea, sailing out of {home}, for which I give thanks.
ship.bounty: , a bounty of {bounty}g resting upon my name

island.haven: The black flag governs it now; no lawful host keeps this book, and hospitality lies dead in its halls.
island.default: {place} prospers under our stewardship — {population} souls, and the door open to every honest traveller.

quiet.ship: Little of note to record — fair passage and courteous ports, for which I am grateful. A calm sea, the proverb says, teaches no sailor wisdom, yet I welcome it gladly.
quiet.island: The season has been peaceable, for which we give thanks. Trade comes and goes, and each guest departs content.

say: {we} came alongside {foe} as a guest comes to a strange door, and departed the richer by {goods} bales and {gold}g, leaving her the poorer but the wiser
{we} relieved {foe} of {goods} crates and {gold}g — a hard trade, yet as they say in {our} country, the sea keeps no ledger of fairness
{we} pressed {foe} until her master yielded, and set {goods} casks and {gold}g into {our} hold before granting her leave to limp for {foeHome}
{foe} rode low and unwary, and {we} lightened her of {goods} chests and {gold}g, then bade her go on to {foeHome} with {our} regrets
{we} took from {foe} what the lanes would bear — {goods} bales and {gold}g — and let the stripped hull carry {our} name home
{we} boarded {foe} with all courtesy and stripped her without it, {goods} crates and {gold}g the measure of the discourtesy
{we} counted {goods} casks and {gold}g out of {foe}, for a merchant knows a cargo's worth to the last coin, even one {we} did not pay for
{foe} struck her colours to {us} rather than be sunk, and {we} took {goods} chests and {gold}g for her life — a bargain she named cruel and {we} called merciful

say: {we} traded shot for shot with {foe} until the sea closed over her and her cargo both — a poor market, where both sides pay
{we} held {foe} under {our} guns until she filled and went down, and all she carried went to the deep unbought
{foe} would not yield, and so {we} sent her under with every bale she owned — the sea is a merchant that pays no one
{we} sank {foe} where she fought, and mourned the honest cargo drowned with her more than the hull
{we} broke {foe} apart at close quarters and watched her go down whole, holds and all, beyond any man's recovering
{foe} chose the deep over the yielding of her flag, and {we} granted her the deep — may it prove a gentler port than any {we} could offer
{we} put {foe} beneath the waves and took nothing for it, for the drowned keep their own accounts
{we} fought {foe} until she settled and slid away, her wealth unspent, her voyage ended far from {foeHome}

say: {foe} bore down on {us} as a wolf upon a laden mule, and learned that even a trader's mule can kick — she went under for the lesson
{we} were no easy guest for {foe}; she came to rob and {we} sent her to the bottom for her discourtesy
{foe} mistook {our} cargo for a gift and {our} crew for cowards, and {we} corrected her on both counts before she sank
{we} turned {foe}'s own boldness against her, and she who came hunting {our} hold now keeps company with the fishes
{foe} raised her black flag against {us}, and {we} answered with iron until the flag and all beneath it went down together
{we} beat {foe} off and then below — a merchant defends his road as a host defends his threshold, to the last
{foe} thought a trader carries goods and no teeth, and {we} showed her the teeth before she showed {us} her keel
{we} would not be robbed and {foe} would not relent, so the matter was settled the only way left — she sank, and {we} sailed on

say: {we} ran {foe} to ground at the edge of the lanes and put an end to her — one fewer wolf between honest ports
{we} chased {foe} out of {foeHome}'s shadow and sank her, and the merchants of these waters will sleep the easier
{foe} had preyed on the peaceable long enough, and {we} brought her the reckoning the lanes had long owed her
{we} hunted {foe} across three days of open water and cut her down at the last — a debt of blood, paid in full
{foe} fled as the guilty flee, and {we} ran her down as duty runs, and left her broken on the swell
{we} caught {foe} at her wicked trade and sank her mid-crime — as they say in {our} country, the thief meets the sea he made
{we} put {foe} under and freed the road she haunted, and no honest man from {foeHome} to home will weep for her
{foe} had grown fat on stolen cargo, and {we} emptied her into the deep where no plunder can follow
